sections.heading: 1. Key Expressions & Sentences Reviewed (Lessons 127–133)
points: Lesson 127: "Mhepo yakavhuvhuta nesimba, miti ikazununguka." — The wind blew strongly, and the trees swayed.
Lesson 128: "Rwizi rwuzere nemvura mushure mekunaya kwanezuro." — The river is full of water after yesterday's rain.
Lesson 129: "Ndiri kuda kuzorora zvishoma ndisati ndaenderera mberi." — I want to rest a little before I continue forward.
Lesson 130: "Mhepo iri kuvhuvhuta zvakasimba kubva kumabvazuva." — The wind is blowing strongly from the east.
Lesson 131: "Uri kunzwa zvakanaka here kana kuti ndoita zvekudaidzira?" — Can you hear me well, or should I speak louder?
Lesson 132: "Ndiri kuenda kubasa izvozvi kuti ndinotanga mazuva angu." — I am going to work right now to start my shift.
Lesson 133: "Zvichiri zvakaoma zvikuru; asi ndinoziva kuti zvichanaka." — It is still quite difficult, but I know that things will get better.

sections.heading: 2. Core Shona Grammar Rules Consolidated
points: Talking About the Past ('yakavhuvhuta'): Recent Today Past: [nda- / wa- / ta- / va-] + verb | Earlier Past: [ndaka- / waka- / taka- / vaka-] + verb
Joining Words with 'ne-' ('and / with') in 'nemvura': ne- + Noun = and / with [Noun] (written as a single word, e.g., sadza nemuriwo = sadza and vegetables)
Actions Happening Right Now: The '-ri ku-' Progressive: [Subject + -ri] + ku-[verb] -> Ndiri kuverenga (I am reading) | Vari kufamba (They are walking) | Mvura iri kunaya (It is raining)
Talking About the Past ('zvakasimba'): Recent Today Past: [nda- / wa- / ta- / va-] + verb | Earlier Past: [ndaka- / waka- / taka- / vaka-] + verb
Talking About the Past ('zvakanaka'): Recent Today Past: [nda- / wa- / ta- / va-] + verb | Earlier Past: [ndaka- / waka- / taka- / vaka-] + verb
Talking About the Past ('zvakaoma'): Recent Today Past: [nda- / wa- / ta- / va-] + verb | Earlier Past: [ndaka- / waka- / taka- / vaka-] + verb

sections.heading: 3. Cultural Context & Practical Usage
points: August Winds ('Mhepo yaNyamavhuvhu') & Swaying Indigenous Trees: The Shona name for the month of August is 'Nyamavhuvhu'—named directly after the verb '-vhuvhuta' ('to blow strongly'), because swirling winds sweep across the plateau in August, shaking the trees ('miti ikazununguka') and blowing away dry winter leaves..

Rivers Filling After Heavy Overnight Rain ('Mushure Mekunaya'): After a night of heavy summer rainfall ('kunaya kwanezuro'), rural streams and rivers ('rwizi') fill bank-to-bank with fresh water, replenishing village wells, dams, and grazing pastures..

Pacing Yourself on a Long Task ('Kuzorora Zvishoma'): Taking a brief breather ('kuzorora zvishoma') before continuing forward ('ndisati ndaenderera mberi') reflects a balanced approach to long journeys and demanding physical work..

Cardinal Directions in Shona: East ('Mabvazuva') & West ('Madokero'): Notice how poetic Shona cardinal directions are! East is 'mabvazuva'—literally 'where the sun comes from' ('kubva' + 'zuva')—while West is 'madokero' ('where the sun sets').

review_exercises.prompt: Unit 19 Review — Grammar Mastery: How do you say 'Although it rained heavily, we arrived home safely'?
options: Kana mvura ikanaya mangwana, hatisi kuenda kumunda.
Kunyangwe mvura yakanaya zvakanyanya, takasvika kumba zvakanaka.
Mvura iri kunaya kunze saka vana vari mumba.
Zuva rakabuda masikati mbatya dzikaoma nekukurumidza.
review_exercises.correct_answer: Kunyangwe mvura yakanaya zvakanyanya, takasvika kumba zvakanaka.
review_exercises.explanation: 'Kunyangwe' means 'although / even though', 'yakanaya' is past tense ('rained'), and 'takasvika' is 'we arrived'.

review_exercises.prompt: Unit 19 Review — Numbers & Colours: Which phrase means 'three white trucks and two black cars'?
options: rori chena imwe nemotokari tsvuku nhatu
makombi maviri chena nemabhazi mana matema
marori machena matatu nemotokari nhema mbiri
shangu nhema mbiri nehembe tsvuku imwe
review_exercises.correct_answer: marori machena matatu nemotokari nhema mbiri
review_exercises.explanation: 'Marori machena matatu' = 'three white trucks' and 'nemotokari nhema mbiri' = 'and two black cars'.

review_exercises.prompt: Unit 19 Review — Locatives & Existence: Which word means 'Inside the wooden bowl there are roasted caterpillars'?
options: Patafura pane mabhuku nezvinyoreso.
Kumusika kune michero nemiriwo mizhinji.
Parutivi pemugwagwa pane miti mirefu.
Mundiro yemuti mune madora akakangwa.
review_exercises.explanation: 'Mu-' ('inside') + 'ndiro yemuti' ('wooden bowl') pairs with 'mune' ('there is inside').

review_exercises.prompt: Unit 19 Review — Conditionals & Reciprocal Verbs: What does 'tikashanda nesimba tichibatsirana' mean?
options: if we work hard helping one another
when they finished working at the market
because he worked alone in the field
before you start writing the examination
review_exercises.correct_answer: if we work hard helping one another
review_exercises.explanation: 'Tikashanda nesimba' = 'if we work with strength/hard', and 'tichibatsirana' ('-an-' reciprocal suffix) = 'helping each other'.

review_exercises.prompt: Unit 19 Review — Cultural & Historical Vocabulary: What does the phrase 'zvivakwa zvematombo' refer to?
options: wooden handles used on farm hoes and shovels
stone structures / buildings of stone (the origin of the name Zimbabwe)
modern traffic lights at city intersections
plastic tanks mounted beside houses to store water
review_exercises.correct_answer: stone structures / buildings of stone (the origin of the name Zimbabwe)

review_exercises.prompt: Unit 19 Review — Translate this new synthesis sentence into English: 'Vanhu vazhinji vari kutengesa michero nemiriwo pamusika.'
options: Our ancestors built stone walls without mortar long ago.
Two women are sitting under an umbrella near the road.
Many people are selling fruits and vegetables at the market.
We are planning to visit our grandparents next month.
review_exercises.correct_answer: Many people are selling fruits and vegetables at the market.
review_exercises.explanation: 'Vanhu vazhinji' = 'Many people', 'vari kutengesa' = 'are selling', 'michero nemiriwo' = 'fruits and vegetables', 'pamusika' = 'at the market'.
